Copy the skills in. Architect, build, then craft.
One command installs AIDDbot. Then you map the system, draft a spec and build the change, and craft lasting quality. Details live in the repo.

Plain markdown. Any agent. No package left behind — the skills travel with the repo.

## Install

Node.js 18 or later, Git, and one agent: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot.

From the root of your repository, run `npx github:AIDDbot/AIDDbot init`.

That copies the skills, adds the agent profiles, and commits them. Files you already have stay untouched. In Codex, start each command with `$`.

## Architect

Open the agent in that folder and map the system: `/architect-initial-foundation`.

Legacy code is scanned. A new system is scaffolded. You approve the foundation and the rules.

## Build

Name the change before anyone codes: `/architect-requested-spec riders can rate a trip from 1 to 5 stars`.

You approve the spec. Nothing is built yet.

Then construct that change: `/build-requested-spec`.

The agents write the code, prove it, and ship a version.

## Craft

Keep the quality maintainable: `/craft-lasting-quality`.

Debt becomes the next repair, so the system lasts.

Four commands. One loop. A version you can trust.
Start a system, draft a change, ship it, or repair the debt. The full rules live in the repository.

You name the outcome. AIDDbot writes the spec, builds the change, and ships it with proof.

Specs before code, so the agent does not invent. Rules in the repo, so the code follows your standards. A second agent checks the work, so you verify instead of hope.

## Four commands

| | You get | Command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Start** | A map of the system and the rules the agent will follow | `/architect-initial-foundation` |
| **Draft** | A spec you approve now and build when you are ready | `/architect-requested-spec` |
| **Ship** | One change, proved and released | `/build-requested-spec` |
| **Repair** | Debt cleared, quality that lasts | `/craft-lasting-quality` |

**Architect** designs. **Builder** writes the code and the tests. **Craftsman** proves the change and ships. The reviewer is never the author.

In Codex, start each command with `$`.
